raw:
# Syntetyzowany raport przeglądu

Recenzent **qwen** nie dostarczył znaleźć. Recenzent **sonnet** dostarczył 15 znaleźć — żadne z nich się nie powtarzają, więc wszystkie są zachowywane.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Arbitrary file read with no path validation
DESCRIPTION: `parse_config` accepts any string path and reads it without restriction. An attacker who controls the `path` argument can read arbitrary files on the filesystem (e.g., `/etc/passwd`, SSH keys, `.env` files). There is no allowlist, no chroot check, and no canonicalization to prevent directory traversal sequences.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Resolve the path with `Path(path).resolve()` and assert it is within an expected base directory before reading; reject or raise on paths that escape the allowed root.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Empty key accepted when line starts with colon
DESCRIPTION: `line.partition(":")` on a line like `: value` yields `key=""`. After stripping, an empty string is used as a dict key (`config[""] = ...`). This silently corrupts the config and can mask real keys if multiple such lines exist, since they all collide on the same empty-string key.
SUGGESTED_FIX: After stripping, check `if not key: continue` (or raise/log) before inserting into `config`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Lines without colon silently stored under empty key
DESCRIPTION: `line.partition(":")` returns `(line, "", "")` when no colon is present. `key` becomes the entire line content, `value` becomes `""`. This means a malformed line like `justakeyword` is inserted as `config["justakeyword"] = ""` rather than being treated as an error, producing silently wrong data.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check that the separator returned by `partition` is non-empty (i.e., `sep == ":"`) before processing; otherwise skip or log the line as malformed.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Negative integers silently stored as strings
DESCRIPTION: `value.isdigit()` returns `False` for negative numbers (e.g., `-42`) because `-` is not a digit character. These values fall through to the `else` branch and are stored as plain strings, breaking any downstream code that expects numeric types for negative config values.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace `value.isdigit()` with a try/except around `int(value)` (checking for the absence of `.`) or use `re.match(r"^-?\d+$", value)`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Float regex rejects negative floats and scientific notation
DESCRIPTION: The regex `^-?\d+\.\d+$` correctly handles negative floats but misses scientific notation like `1e10`, `1.5e-3`, or `1.5E+3`, which are valid Python/YAML float representations. Such values silently become strings. Additionally, values like `1.` or `.5` (partial decimal notation) are rejected despite being valid in many contexts.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use a `try/except` approach: attempt `float(value)` after ruling out integers, and catch `ValueError` to fall back to string storage.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Values containing colons truncated incorrectly
DESCRIPTION: `line.partition(":")` splits on the *first* colon only, which is correct, but `value` is everything after that first colon unmodified. A value like `http://example.com` will parse as `key="http"`, `value="//example.com"` — splitting on the wrong colon and silently corrupting both key and value.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `line.split(":", 1)` and treat the remainder as the value, or document that colons in values require quoting and validate accordingly.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: All exceptions silently swallowed, no logging or line info
DESCRIPTION: Both the outer `except Exception: return config` and the inner `except Exception: pass` discard all error information. A corrupted file, permission error, or encoding issue produces an empty or partial dict with no indication of what went wrong. The `line_num` variable is computed but never used.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Log or re-raise meaningful errors (at minimum use `logging.warning`), and incorporate `line_num` into any per-line error messages to aid debugging.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: No file size limit before reading entire file into memory
DESCRIPTION: `Path(path).read_text()` loads the entire file at once. A very large file (intentionally or accidentally) will exhaust available memory before any parsing begins, enabling a denial-of-service scenario in any environment where `path` can be influenced externally.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check `Path(path).stat().st_size` against a reasonable maximum before calling `read_text()`, or read the file line-by-line with a hard cap on total bytes processed.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: No encoding specified; behavior is platform-dependent
DESCRIPTION: `Path(path).read_text()` uses the platform default encoding (often `locale.getpreferredencoding()`), which differs between Linux, Windows, and macOS. Config files with non-ASCII characters (e.g., UTF-8 comments or values) may raise `UnicodeDecodeError` or silently mis-decode on some platforms.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Pass an explicit `encoding="utf-8"` (and optionally `errors="replace"` or `errors="strict"`) to `read_text()`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Duplicate keys silently overwritten, last value wins
DESCRIPTION: If a config file contains the same key multiple times, each occurrence silently replaces the previous value. There is no warning or error. This can mask typos or configuration mistakes that produce subtle, hard-to-diagnose runtime behaviour.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Detect duplicate keys by checking `if key in config` before assignment and either raising a `ValueError` or emitting a warning via `logging`.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `merge_configs` silently returns partial result on missing file
DESCRIPTION: If either `base_path` or `override_path` does not exist (or cannot be read), `parse_config` returns an empty dict silently. `merge_configs` then proceeds with incomplete data and returns a result that looks valid but is missing an entire config layer, with no indication to the caller.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Either propagate exceptions from `parse_config` for missing files, or have `merge_configs` verify both paths exist before calling `parse_config` and raise a descriptive error if they do not.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Whitespace-only lines not reliably skipped
DESCRIPTION: `line = raw.strip()` followed by `if not line` does correctly skip whitespace-only lines. However, lines consisting solely of tab characters mixed with other Unicode whitespace rely on Python's `str.strip()` stripping all Unicode whitespace, which is correct but undocumented as an explicit design choice — worth noting since some YAML-like parsers treat tabs as errors.
SUGGESTED_FIX: No code change required, but add a comment or docstring note clarifying that tabs and all Unicode whitespace are treated as line delimiters/ignored content.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Boolean coercion is case-insensitive but undocumented
DESCRIPTION: `value.lower() in ("true", "false")` accepts `True`, `TRUE`, `TrUe`, etc. This is wider than standard YAML (which only allows `true`/`false` lowercase). While arguably convenient, the behaviour is undocumented and may surprise users expecting strict YAML semantics.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Document the accepted boolean literals explicitly in the docstring, or restrict to lowercase-only matching if strict YAML compatibility is required.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: data
TITLE: Type annotation `dict` is unparameterized
DESCRIPTION: The return type is annotated as `dict` rather than `dict[str, int | float | bool | str]`. This gives static analysis tools (mypy, pyright) no information about the key/value types, reducing the usefulness of type checking for callers.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `dict[str, int | float | bool | str]` (Python 3.10+) or `Dict[str, Union[int, float, bool, str]]` from `typing` for older versions.

---END---

DESCRIPTION: If either `base_path` or `override_path` does not exist (or cannot be read), `parse_config` returns an empty dict silently. `merge_configs` then proceeds with incomplete data and returns a result that looks valid but is missing an entire config layer, with no indication to the caller.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Either propagate exceptions from `parse_config` for missing files, or have `merge_configs` verify both paths exist before calling `parse_config` and raise a descriptive error if they do not.

findings.title: Whitespace-only lines not reliably skipped
findings.description: `line = raw.strip()` followed by `if not line` does correctly skip whitespace-only lines. However, lines consisting solely of tab characters mixed with other Unicode whitespace rely on Python's `str.strip()` stripping all Unicode whitespace, which is correct but undocumented as an explicit design choice — worth noting since some YAML-like parsers treat tabs as errors.
findings.suggested_fix: No code change required, but add a comment or docstring note clarifying that tabs and all Unicode whitespace are treated as line delimiters/ignored content.

findings.title: Boolean coercion is case-insensitive but undocumented
findings.description: `value.lower() in ("true", "false")` accepts `True`, `TRUE`, `TrUe`, etc. This is wider than standard YAML (which only allows `true`/`false` lowercase). While arguably convenient, the behaviour is undocumented and may surprise users expecting strict YAML semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the accepted boolean literals explicitly in the docstring, or restrict to lowercase-only matching if strict YAML compatibility is required.

findings.title: Type annotation `dict` is unparameterized
findings.description: The return type is annotated as `dict` rather than `dict[str, int | float | bool | str]`. This gives static analysis tools (mypy, pyright) no information about the key/value types, reducing the usefulness of type checking for callers.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `dict[str, int | float | bool | str]` (Python 3.10+) or `Dict[str, Union[int, float, bool, str]]` from `typing` for older versions.
